edits.old:
Lean Body Mass Calculator

Splits total body weight into lean mass and fat mass. Boer (1984) is the primary formula; James (1976) and Hume (1966) provide the comparison — typical spread is under 2 kg for average bodies, wider for heavier individuals.

Best for: Athletes, fitness enthusiasts, and anyone tracking body composition

Example: A 5'8" male weighing 170 lbs has an estimated lean body mass of approximately 141 lbs (Boer formula), meaning about 29 lbs (~17%) of his weight is fat — within the healthy range for men.
Try Calculator →
edits.new:
Lean Body Mass Calculator

Splits total body weight into lean mass and fat mass. Boer (1984) is the primary formula; James (1976) and Hume (1966) provide the comparison — typical spread is under 2 kg for average bodies, wider for heavier individuals.

Best for: Athletes, fitness enthusiasts, and anyone tracking body composition

Example: A 5'8" male weighing 170 lbs has an estimated lean body mass of approximately 141 lbs (Boer formula), meaning about 29 lbs (~17%) of his weight is fat — within the healthy range for men.
Try Calculator →

Body Fat Calculator

Estimates body fat percentage three ways — tape measure (Navy method), skinfold calipers (Jackson–Pollock) or height and weight (Deurenberg) — shows how far apart the methods land, and ranks your result against CDC body scans of US adults.

Best for: Estimating body fat at home, or sanity-checking a smart-scale or caliper reading

Example: A 35-year-old man, 5'10", with a 15.5-inch neck and a 35-inch waist comes out at 18.5% by the tape method — 94% of US men aged 30–39 have more body fat on CDC scans. See every age group on the body fat percentage chart.
Try Calculator →
